topic: A new zero-in-degree condemnation candidate discovered during DEFER is d
canonical_claim: A new zero-in-degree condemnation candidate discovered during DEFER is detected only at the next FOLD, delaying reclaim by at most the bounded defer window but never deleting an uncondemned blob.

topic: The GC acceptance criteria require idle rounds to perform no generation-
canonical_claim: The GC acceptance criteria require idle rounds to perform no generation-run reads or writes, small-delta rounds to amortize snapshot rebuilds, default behavior to remain unchanged except for idle skipping, and `dangling == 0` in unit and live validation.

topic: `graduationDue` returns true for a retired entry with `delete_pending` o
canonical_claim: `graduationDue` returns true for a retired entry with `delete_pending` or `condemn_round < min_ack`; a missing retired list also returns true to force the existing fail-closed fold path rather than silently deferring.

topic: A lower `observed_gc_round` caused by syncer lag is conservative because
canonical_claim: A lower `observed_gc_round` caused by syncer lag is conservative because `computeHeartbeatFloor` takes the minimum acknowledgement across live heartbeats; lag can hold the floor back but cannot advance it beyond an installed round.

topic: At steady state after driving GC to an idle deferred round, S34 measured
canonical_claim: At steady state after driving GC to an idle deferred round, S34 measured zero discovery `CasRootGet` operations for iteration counts from 5 through 40 and flat `root_dirs = 2`.

topic: Under S27 duplicate-key and dropped-continuation-token LIST anomalies, G
canonical_claim: Under S27 duplicate-key and dropped-continuation-token LIST anomalies, GC tolerated 40 perturbed LISTs with zero round errors, replica agreement, `dangling=0`, and dropped-content reclamation; unstable listings increased `CasRootGet` from 74 to 1373 as GC conservatively re-read.

topic: `isPrecommitDead(uint64_t writer_epoch, uint64_t build_sequence, const M
canonical_claim: `isPrecommitDead(uint64_t writer_epoch, uint64_t build_sequence, const MountLease & w)` must be shared by reclaim and discover paths; a future epoch is live, an older epoch is dead, and an equal epoch is dead only when the retired sentinel or `min_active > build_sequence` applies.

topic: Force-Read is strictly more reading than Skip and therefore cannot under
canonical_claim: Force-Read is strictly more reading than Skip and therefore cannot under-count in-degree; each abandoned precommit adds at most one forced revisit at the round its build sequence crosses the floor.

topic: The resurrect supersede produces one retired entry per hash, drops the s
canonical_claim: The resurrect supersede produces one retired entry per hash, drops the stale token entry, preserves hash order, and commits the replacement through the existing R5 round CAS.

topic: A fresh upload is condemned only when the hash has been referenced, the
canonical_claim: A fresh upload is condemned only when the hash has been referenced, the current object exists, and its folded current in-degree is zero; never-referenced uploads are not condemned.

topic: The CA cache disk shares the base disk's metadata-bound disk identity fo
canonical_claim: The CA cache disk shares the base disk's metadata-bound disk identity for GC scheduling and `system.content_addressed_log` attribution, so two disk names correspond to one GC identity.

topic: retained-views-not-reachability-state
canonical_claim: Mutable files are not reachability state, and retained views hold no tokens with authority, do not affect GC in-degree, and do not protect objects from garbage collection. Additionally, GC journal trimming and abandoned-precommit reclaim do not change committed `root.refs`, so they do not invalidate part-folder views. Additionally, Cached views are not owner state, do not affect in-degree, and do not protect objects from GC.

topic: GC journal-only mutations do not route through the facade and do not inv
canonical_claim: GC journal-only mutations do not route through the facade and do not invalidate retained views because they do not change committed refs or committed `RootRef::mutable_files`.

topic: A durable precommit closure cannot be deleted by GC once a per-shard sea
canonical_claim: A durable precommit closure cannot be deleted by GC once a per-shard seal after precommitAdd folds the closure edge, because d becomes at least one and the entry is spared.

topic: The per-shard seal is taken when the target shard is read, not once glob
canonical_claim: The per-shard seal is taken when the target shard is read, not once globally for the whole GC pass; the edge theorem still holds because the closure is stored in that target shard's journal.

topic: A blob condemned after precommitAdd is doomed to be spared at the next f
canonical_claim: A blob condemned after precommitAdd is doomed to be spared at the next fold, while a blob already graduated before precommitAdd must be detected by the writer and displaced with a fresh incarnation.

topic: GC condemn captures the body token and writes condemned meta, spare CASe
canonical_claim: GC condemn captures the body token and writes condemned meta, spare CASes condemned to clean, and delete removes the body by exact token before deleting the meta; there is no tombstone handshake in v3.

topic: Mass-DROP metadata operations must use a bounded parallel pool because o
canonical_claim: Mass-DROP metadata operations must use a bounded parallel pool because one million sequential metadata CASes at about 20 ms each would take roughly 5.5 hours.

topic: GC writes condemned metadata at condemn, clears it at spare, deletes it
canonical_claim: GC writes condemned metadata at condemn, clears it at spare, deletes it after exact-token body deletion, and performs per-hash metadata operations on a bounded parallel pool.

topic: GC deletion in the raw-body design is a tombstone handshake
canonical_claim: GC deletion in the raw-body design is a tombstone handshake: transition meta from `condemned` to `tombstone`, delete the body, then delete the tombstone meta, using a bounded parallel pool.

topic: A GC delete may delete a body only after winning the `condemned` to `tom
canonical_claim: A GC delete may delete a body only after winning the `condemned` to `tombstone` CAS; the terminal tombstone prevents a writer from re-establishing the body after that claim.

topic: The destructive path fails closed
canonical_claim: The destructive path fails closed: GC never deletes a body without a won tombstone claim, while a 404 during fold is recorded and continued rather than throwing or fail-closing the fold.

topic: GC condemns a clean meta by CASing it to condemned and stores the result
canonical_claim: GC condemns a clean meta by CASing it to condemned and stores the resulting condemned-meta etag in `RetiredEntry.token`; it spares by CASing condemned to clean and ignores absent or tombstone metas during the condemn pass.

topic: GC supersede detection re-reads meta for net-zero-touched entries and co
canonical_claim: GC supersede detection re-reads meta for net-zero-touched entries and compares the current meta etag with the stored condemned-meta etag; a mismatch means the retired entry refers to a newer incarnation.

topic: The GC rebuild skips `
canonical_claim: The GC rebuild skips `.meta` keys in the `blobs/` listing, captures or repairs the corresponding meta for each body, and stores the condemned-meta etag rather than the body token in rebuilt retired state.

topic: After a successful ref-fold adoption, consumed `_log` objects may be del
canonical_claim: After a successful ref-fold adoption, consumed `_log` objects may be deleted in bounded batches; an interrupted post-CAS deletion leaves only physical debris and is not a second protocol phase.

topic: A productive ref handoff is forced by fold-delta threshold, ref-tail pre
canonical_claim: A productive ref handoff is forced by fold-delta threshold, ref-tail pressure, maximum defer age, destructive demand, or `remove_namespace`; a deferred round still replays the complete tail for destructive protection.

topic: After a successful `gc/state` CAS, GC deletes covered ref-log objects wi
canonical_claim: After a successful `gc/state` CAS, GC deletes covered ref-log objects with exact-key batch deletes of at most 1000 keys per request; if the CAS loses, it deletes no ref-log object.

topic: retired-snapshot-unchanged-semantics
canonical_claim: Settlement semantics remain byte-for-byte unchanged in the retired-in-snapshot plan: condemn, carry, graduate with `delete_pending`, redelete, clamp suppression, pre-CAS single delete site, resurrect-supersede, `.meta` writes, B170 events, and GC-log counters are preserved. Additionally, The retired-in-snapshot design keeps B170 events, GC-log counters, `.meta` writes, and the `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log` schema unchanged.

topic: carried-condemned-settlement
canonical_claim: A carried condemned sentinel is settlement-only: it never sets the merge touch bit, emits no zero marker, and does not trigger `peek_head` when carry is the only activity. Additionally, Fresh condemns emit `kCondemned` rows, absent-at-condemn cases emit `kZeroMarker` as before, prior zero markers are dropped on carry, and carried condemned rows do not set `cur_touched`. Additionally, A carried `kCondemned` row is settlement-only and must not set the merge touch bit; only real edges or deltas touching a blob may trigger a zero marker or a resurrect-supersede `peek_head` probe.
